questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Opportunities for Korean language learning

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Sogang provided a lot of info, and it was easy to prepare most information from home before arriving

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No specific assistance other than information via email

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was clear who to contact in different instances and the orientation days were helpful

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got help from people I know, and could stay for cheap in an apartment of someone I know, but it might have been difficult if I didnt

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Consider the route to school like public transit etc. And get Korean friends to check any listings for signs of scams

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Cant say as I didnt live in the campus dorms but I heard mixed reviews of it

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They sent information beforehand and your login information that you need to register

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emails beforehand

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the class I wanted :) but you have to be super fast

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Consider the time difference if you do the registration from Denmark. It might be in the night like 4 am. And check the course catalogues from the year before to prepare for which classes you want. If you're going in Fall semester I would recommend checking the last Fall semester for classes, not Spring semester as Spring and Fall classes often differ. 
When you do the registration, its quick to type in the class course CODE instead of the title of the class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took one course apart from the Language Program so I only have one reference of the academic level but it was a bit easier than I thought. But I think I feared a very high level so I thought it was appropriate!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Same amount of readings but more lecture style than what we have in Korean studies in UCPH. Not a lot of back and forth between professor and students, more just either lecture style or student presentations with very short feedback from prof..

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Diffusion of the K-wave (2,5 hrs a week)
KAP200 Korean Language (20 hrs a week)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I recommend both to Korean studies students!!
Diffusion of the K-wave is good if you have an interest or knowledge about Korean popular media

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
The national Korean health insurance was mandatory and a bit more expensive than I expected. You can opt out of it only if you can prove you have a health insurance from your home country that covers ALL THE SAME THINGS. !! it might not be accepted if it doesnt cover certain things.

And if you are sick and go to the hospital, the fees are pretty expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
hospital, insurance: more
food, shopping: less

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I cant say much as i didnt join any clubs but there were club days where you could see all the clubs and ask questions/join etc. I heard good things though!!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were many activities for the exchange students!! They were hosted by "HUG" the exchange student club where you can meet many Korean and non-korean students. There were sports, cultural, cooking, theatre, dinner, talent show
etc.etc
.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely join the HUG activities! And join from the beginning so you get to know people. If you start joining them too late it might feel like people are already close imo

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking, cultural and traditional things, travel domestically

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Since I study Korean culture, it wasn't that difficult

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Meet your buddy, join HUG activities

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Consider that sometimes you might be in a place where no one speaks English.
Elders are very respected and you should always make room for them.
You might feel stared at sometimes, but i think people are mostly just curious :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The respect between everyone, the love for food and sharing food, the Korean 정

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use all the opportunities you are given, like joining clubs and events
Consider opening a bank account if you want to shop online etc
Its a really great uni and a great location!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe think about how you're gonna get a SIM-card/Korean phone number before you arrive so you're not stuck with no data right away (though the public wifi is good)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning a lot of the language and trying new things, understanding the culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing your family, friends and everything you are familiar with at home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
